trigger: The user rejected the first post-rejection anchor concept because it still differed materially from the project-source completed-screen image baseline.

visualMismatchFindings.finding: The candidate changed the art style from warm pixel-art chibi cats to dark painterly high-fantasy catfolk.
The candidate omitted the persistent source-baseline information architecture: player/resource header, contextual screen header, and five-tab bottom navigation.
The candidate replaced the bright tower-town, shop-management and playful recruitment presentation with generic gothic RPG scenes.
The candidate was presented as a 2x2 collage rather than individual portrait mobile screens at the target composition and density.
The battle, boss and gacha screens did not preserve the source-baseline pixel-art silhouette language, brown-and-gold framing, compact modular HUD, or playful capsule-machine identity.
Generated Japanese labels and values were not controlled enough for a production mockup and cannot be accepted as final UI evidence.

pixel-art chibi cats, enemies, town, shops and tower scenes
contextual screen title and status header
screen-specific scene composition instead of generic RPG panels

Create one individual portrait anchor screen at a time, starting with the primary tower-lobby or battle screen.
